acceptanceCriteria: Relative specifiers are classified by whole path segment in both places.
A regression case with a dot-prefixed alias selects the importer and fails without the fix.
body: Codex review round 8 of the V1-0958 lane (issue 659, branch claude/gh659 head 2ea2d8ac): internal/contextindex/webresolve.go Resolve (~line 95) and buildWebImportGraph (~line 1103) treat any specifier starting with `.` as relative, but TypeScript counts a specifier as relative only when it matches ^\.\.?($|/). Reproduction: tsconfig `paths: {".generated/*": ["./src/generated/*"]}` and `import ... from ".generated/client"`; impact on src/generated/client.ts misses the importer and adds no UNKNOWN disclosure. Expected: whole-segment relative classification, alias applied. Leave the rule (c) oracle in reverseimports.go:163 alone unless GPK-V0-027 is amended.

Evidence: docs/build-log/2026-10-08-v1-0967-dot-prefixed-alias.md and docs/build-log/2026-10-08-batch-i-integration.md at that commit (each digest is that file’s sha256); the build logs record the focused tests and limits. title: impact: dot-prefixed bare tsconfig aliases are treated as relative and miss their dependants without disclosure (V1-0958 review P2)
